page: UpCloud GPU-32xCPU-384GB-3xL4 is a GPU-accelerated server instance built on the KVM hypervisor and x86_64 CPU architecture. The system features 32 shared vCPUs paired with 384.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 12.0 GB of RAM per core. Acceleration is driven by three NVIDIA L4 GPUs from the Ada Lovelace family, providing a combined total of 72 GB of VRAM.

This server configuration does not include local storage, requiring external storage attachments for persistent data. The CPU allocation is shared, which represents a potential performance tradeoff for workloads requiring sustained, non-blocking CPU execution. Qualitatively, the combination of a high-capacity memory footprint and triple GPU accelerators on a shared CPU model offers a specialized resource profile, balancing high-density GPU and memory capacity against shared compute resources.

The hardware composition is designed for workloads that rely heavily on GPU acceleration and large memory capacities rather than dedicated, continuous CPU cycles. Appropriate workloads include machine learning inference, data science jobs, distributed graphics rendering, and memory-intensive analytical processing.
